verdicts.evidence: The locator's cache is bypassed and the file re-read on every call. Within one command run the mission is not written between two lookups, so every answer is the same. Measured: 121 command runs byte-identical; the only differing direct case (1 of 25) is the one built to show the cache exists, where the file is rewritten between two calls of the same locator, which no command does. Survived the CI unit pass on this branch and the whole-net pass of 2026-09-29 (scripts/mutation-wholenet.mjs, seven legs, serial). Measurement: identical on all 11 missions × 11 commands (121 runs); 1 of 25 direct calls differ. Probe suite 2026-09-28 (scratch recipe, reproduced in the PR): eleven missions built with the pristine 0.42.3-dev build — `init` (blank), `init --example`, and the example with a dead pointer, the regulated tier on, a drifted seal, an edited and a removed rule, a failing after-hook, no scaffold-lock (unrecorded corpus), an under-filled framing note, a DRAFT ADR, and a fresh mission with two agent ratifications. Each mutant was spliced alone into dist/lib and eleven commands were run on each mission (check with and without --strict, --json, --sarif, --hooks; gate-hook for claude, cursor and gemini), exit code, stdout and stderr compared byte for byte with the pristine build. Positive control: the killed mutants gate-hook L77 and sarif L161 applied the same way differ on the regulated mission.
